text: Git branching is an important part of version control. A branch lets you work on new ideas without changing the main code. Developers often create feature branches to add a new function or fix a problem. When the work is finished, they merge the branch back into the main project. Before merging, teams usually open a pull request so others can review the changes. This workflow keeps the project safe and organised. If something goes wrong, you can simply delete the branch and try again. Learning how branches work helps you collaborate with others and manage your code more confidently.
